# Frozen native and isolated Python execution baselines

**Goal.** Establish reproducible optimized scalar-native and explicit Python-child cost evidence on the common Wave 24 base. Wave 23 removed eager Python linkage; its matrix benchmark intentionally used an older frozen base and cannot describe the new boundary.

**Exclusive ownership.** `bench/**`. Do not edit compiler/runtime/notebook/foreign/bridge/bind/LibTorch crates, root Cargo files, shared documents, or hidden holdout materials. Do not consume concurrent conditionals or loader improvements. Preserve historical reports.

## Deliverable and contract

1. Add a bounded public harness with explicit release builds by default, exact source revision/build flags/toolchain/binary hashes, library linkage and interpreter provenance, and reproducible raw reports. Externally supplied binaries require verified build provenance or an unverified-profile label. Use separate build/temporary directories so concurrent chats cannot overwrite measured binaries. Record source/package hashes, commands, inputs, environment/thread controls, warmups, repetitions, deadlines, CPU/wall/peak RSS, and exclusions.
2. Cover two distinct cases using only already committed syntax: a deterministic scalar arithmetic/range-loop program built by `cgx2c`, compared with an equivalent optimized Rust executable; and an explicit allowlisted copied-scalar Python call (e.g. `math.isqrt` with exact integer inputs) through `cgx2 run`, compared with the same selected CPython performing the same computation in a fresh `-I -S` process. Label the Python baseline's omitted CGx2 parsing/checking/protocol validation. Measure `check`, native build, and already-built native execution separately; the ordinary `cgx2 run` interpreter is not the ahead-of-time native executable. Report child startup/transport costs as included or unmeasured rather than subtracting unrelated timings.
3. Freeze paired inputs and process controls, preregister at least 30 independent execution process pairs per case with deterministic randomized order and at least five independent build/check runs if intervals are reported for those phases. Verify outputs/errors before accepting timings, prevent compiler constant folding from eliminating the chosen work, retain every failed/timed-out run, and report uncertainty with the sample unit correctly stated. Require at least 20 completed samples for p95; label RSS high-water marks and timer resolution. No p99 or broad inference/GPU/LLM claim.
4. Prove exact default native executable and native CLI have no libpython ELF dependency; retain sampled maps and demonstrate only the explicit Python case launches a worker. Record the selected interpreter executable/version/prefix and the local unpinned identity. Check error categories/empty output for negative `isqrt`, wrong return shape, and missing interpreter, then verify a subsequent good run. Neither benchmark execution nor an override should silently fall back in process.
5. Keep retained in-process PyO3 and isolated-worker results separate. This lane does not score the old tiny-call-versus-PyO3 target with a subprocess comparison, claim they have equivalent overhead, or rewrite a target after seeing results. General native runtime/RSS thresholds apply only to the stated selected workload observations and do not establish a whole-language release gate. Genuine paired model/human evidence remains unrun. Avoid expanding benchmark task datasets or touching private answers.

## Verification and handoff

Add meaningful harness tests for wrong output, missing binary/interpreter, timeout/nonzero exit, build provenance, sample gates, randomized paired accounting, and failure retention. Run all benchmark tests and public syntax readiness against the frozen compiler. Preserve the base toolchain lock; if the existing build recipe path cannot be written, build the same pinned compiler locally and pass `--compiler`, retaining the failed attempt if one occurred. Commit preregistration, raw successful/failed observations, analysis with clear route labels and limitations, and exact rerun commands under bench. Report files, checks and commit, then stop for review.
